newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - April 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - April 10.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

An exclusive survey by The Australian Financial Review and the Australian Stock Exchange shows the mining and industrial sectors have dominated Corporate Australia's profit performance in the first six months of 1996/97. Mining stocks have slumped, and a a result investors have dumped mining stocks, reducing the value of the sector by 10 per cent. Meanwhile, industrials have enjoyed steady profits. Page 1.

The Wallis inquiry has paved the way for further competition in Australia's banking industry from both domestic and international forces, yet consumers may find that under recommendations for banks to stop subsidising some services, they will find account transactions more expensive. Page 1.

Following discussion with independent directors indicating its initial bid for radio network Austereo Ltd would not be accepted, Village Roadshow has been forced to raise its bid 20 cents a share to A$2.55 a share for the 47 per cent of Austereo it does not own. The raised bid was greeted
well, with independent directors recommending shareholders accept the deal. Page 21.

An internal BHP document prepared this week shows that in an attempt to contain costs and push new projects, the Big Australian will quit grassroots exploration in up to 12 countries, including Papua New Guinea, Indonesia and the Philippines. The document indicated gold and copper will be the main thrust of BHP's exploration program. Page 21.

The successful completion of Highlands Pacific Ltd's underwriting agreement for its A$190 million float schedule displays renewed faith in Papua New Guinea following its recent civil unrest. The company secured a good spread of sub-underwriters both in Astralia and Papua New Guinea and from international sources. Page 21.

Despite its one-off restructuring costs of A$2.97 million, jewellery retailer Angus & Coote (Holdings) Ltd posted a 57.5 per cent jump in interim net profit to A$2.97 million. However, the company has delayed payment of an interim dividend
due to tough trading conditions and an uncertain outlook. Page 21.
THE AUSTRALIAN

While consumer groups warned the Wallis inquiry into Australia's financial system may erode customer protection, the report was well received by the financial industry. The Australian Consumer Association said it was concerned about the proposed transfer of consumer protection power from the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission to the new
Corporations and Financial Services Commission. Page 21.

The Federal Government's retention of the Factor (f) pharmaceuticals scheme has boosted Australia's position in the race to win the rights as the manufacturing base for Glaxo Wellcome's anti-influenza drug. The drug was developed locally, based on an iniial discovery by CSIRO scientist Dr Peter Colman, and could fetch Glaxo Wellcome A$1 billion in annual sales. Page 21.

More than A$270 million in bank shares were traded yesterday, as investors digested the Federal Government's reaction to the Wallis inquiry not to allow mergers among the big banks. Shares in National Australia Bank and the Commonwealth Bank lifted as oportunities for the two suspected predators to take over the ANZ Bank or Westpac diminished. Page 21.

Under the terms of a non-cash transaction announced yesterday, Joseph Gutnick's Mt Kersey Mining NL will acquire RTZ-CRA's 100 per cent stake in the Snake Hill nickel sulphide project tenements in Western Australia. Mt Kersey will additionally earn its entitlement to as much as 60 per cent of the Lake Ballard joint venture with Delta Gold NL. Page 22.

Despite a lift in turnover in the latest quarter from A$98.5 million to A$102.3 million, North Flinders Mines Ltd has reported a four per cent fall in net profit to A$26.24 million for the nine months to the end of March. Production and profit for the quarter were higher than that of the previous December quarter, but are not expected to be as robust in the June quarter. Page 22.

All airlines, including Qantas Airways and Ansett International, will be affected by user charges at the new A$26 billion Chek Lap Kok airport in Hong Kong, despite persistent lobbying by the airline industry's peak groups. However, leaving Hong Kong is not an option for either Qantas or Ansett, especially Ansett, who uses Hong Kong as a crucial market in its smaller international operations. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

After Federal Treasurer Peter Costello said yesterday he would ignore the recommendation of the Wallis inquiry and maintain controls on mergers between the big four banks, investors savaged potential takeover targets ANZ Bank and Westpac, with both banks selling down yesterday - Westpac down 20 cents to A$6.67, and ANZ down 11 cents to A$7.89. Page 29.

As Federal Treasurer Peter Costello maintained the ban on big bank mergers yesterday, he relaxed the Government's policy on foreign takeovers, and ANZ Bank and Westpac are seen as the main targets. However, the list of potential overseas suitors is only short, as the prices may be too high for them. Page 29.

With the removal of the six pillars policy prohibiting mergers between Australia's big four banks and two largest life insurers AMP and National Mutual, the way is open for AMP to take over a bank, or its rival National Mutual. AMP chief executive George Trumball said the company did not see any need to takeover a bank, but would look at having a tilt at National Mutual. Page 29.

Figures provided in documents to the Australian Stock Exchange ahead of tomorrow's listing of Stadium Australia's securities reveal the four underwriters to the new Olympic Stadium sold only 10,782 of the 34,400 gold packages they had on offer for six months as A$10,000 each. Page 31.

As the deadline for expressions of interest in the Australian National rail assets expire today, the Federal Government may need to act as a matchmaker in the sale, which is expected to fetch more than A$100 million. The Government, the Office of Asset Sales, and advisers Deutsche Morgan Grenfell are
keen to have the deal finalised by the end of June in line with the Government's budget strategy. Page 31.

Despite reports yesterday that the Foreign Investment Review Board had recommended Canadian company CanWest Global Communications CGSs TO sell down its 76 per cent economic interest in the Ten Network to 15 per cent, CanWest head Izzy Asper is continuing to fight to maintain the 76 per cent share. Asper will arrive in Australia soon to meet with senior politicians to discuss the issue. Page 31.
THE AGE

Analysts say the ANZ Bank and Westpac look to be the most likely takeover targets following Wallis inquiry recommendations to allow foreign takeovers of Australian banks. It is believed Lloyds TSB of the United Kingdom and ABN-Amro of the Netherlands would be the most likely bidders. Page C1.

Under the Wallis inquiry blueprint, the number of financial regulators in Australia would be reduced from four to three, with the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission's powers of consumer protection in the financial system transferred to a beefe up version of the Australian Securities Commission. Page C1.

Yesterday's preliminary response by the Federal Government to the Wallis inquiry - a formal response is expected in May after Cabinet considers its position - confirms and enhances the power Federal Treasurer Peter Costello will have over the
finance sector. Page C1.

As Adelaide Steamship shareholders voted yesterday to allow a float of the company's debt-ridden 122-year-old marine business, chief operating officer David Ryan admitted the board would not proceed with the float immediately but that float preparations were well advanced. Page C2.

Hit by post-Wallis inquiry fever and a positive sentiment across the index, Australia's All Ordinaries index rose 20.3 points to 2389.2, its highest level in a month. Vinton Smith Brokerage's Simon Gamble said the jitters of last month could be in the past, and the market seems prepared to move forward. Page C2.

After attacking Westpac Bank for jumping the gun on the Wallis report, Federal Treasurer Peter Costello said the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission would assist in guiding the Federal Government's response to Westpac's A$1.44
billion bid for the Bank of Melbourne. Page C5.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
